title: BLLM: The Entropy Cost of Sound Self-Improvement and a Typed Crossing Network Tested on Five Open Problems: paper, Lean 4 formalization and verification code
description:
A BLLM is a language model that keeps a modification of itself only after a randomized check of soundness epsilon accepts it. The paper proves that certifying modifications of total cost A with at most theta expected false acceptances costs (A/log(1/epsilon))(H(p) + log(1/theta)) up to an additive A, where H(p) is the entropy of the cost profile; that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when the sum of a_n log(1/a_n) converges; and that a proposer needs at least exp(H_{1/2}(pi)) proposals, a bound that language models miss by factors of 1.5 to 4.3. It also describes and measures a typed crossing network with shared memory, run on five open problems (the Yang-Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture and Erdos problem 1183): the network reaches what its libraries can reach with half the checks, Hebbian boosters add nothing, and none of the five problems is solved. The lattice mass gap for four-dimensional SU(2) on beta_W < 1/3 is proved in the paper and has not been refereed.

preprintBeyondTheLLM/ holds the paper as a PDF; BLLM/paper/ holds the REVTeX source with its figures; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip and the arXiv tarball. BLLM/lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib project with fifty-nine theorems, each depending only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. BLLM/checks/ contains independent checks in Python, C and C++ (55,271 checks); BLLM/checks/run_all.sh runs them and builds the Lean project. The benchmark, the crossing network and the logs of every run are in the package eBLLM, version 2.0.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23455686.
